subject: POC: schedule alignment for hands-on & capacity planning (routing, load test windows)

Subject: POC: schedule alignment for hands-on & capacity planning (routing, load test windows)

Hi Alyssa —

Great to meet last week. Per our conversation, we want to lock in two sessions for the Lumina POC: 1) a hands-on working session (prompt review, routing rules, quick prompt engineering) and 2) a capacity planning session to decide Hosted vs Dedicated trial, quota bumps, and token budgets before the load test.

Suggested plan (90m + 60m):
- Day 1 (Hands-on): review prompts, validate routing to the model variant, sanity check KV/prefix caching.
- Day 2 (Capacity): token budget walkthrough, rate limit windows, Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation and quota bump timeline.
- Separate: coordinated 2-hour load test window later in the POC once quotas are bumped.

Can you confirm availability for either of these pairs of slots next week?
- Option A: Tue 5/11 10:00–11:30 PT (Hands-on) + Wed 5/12 10:00–11:00 PT (Capacity)
- Option B: Wed 5/12 14:00–15:30 PT (Hands-on) + Thu 5/13 09:00–10:00 PT (Capacity)

Ben, Marissa — looping you in for capacity input and to prep the POC-capacity-guidelines.pdf (attached). Marcus, if you have quick notes on token budgets that we should surface, will add to the capacity agenda.

Alyssa, if you prefer a single combined 2.5hr session instead, say so and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,

— Jordan

Tom / all —

Adding quick operational numbers so we can lock agenda items:
- Recommended token budgets (starter): chat endpoint 25M tokens/day, completion endpoint 10M tokens/day, embeddings 1.5M units/day. These are conservative for a 2-week POC and allow a 2-hour weekend load spike.
- Rate limits: suggest soft throttle at 120 req/s, hard throttle at 250 req/s for the test window.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: for the full weekend stress run we recommend Dedicated (predictable throughput and isolation). For prompt review and early dev we can run on Hosted with a temporary quota bump.

I attached a quick token_budget_calc.csv with the math and a link to an ops rota for the weekend (ops lead: marcus.lin@redwood.com).
